chapter_seo_title: The Two Throws: Surviving a Thousand Dao-Soldiers in Immortal Wu Jiang’s Estate
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning and the party face a thousand-strong demonic Dao-soldier formation. A bodyguard’s two deadly throws turn the tide, but a second wave of ten thousand appears. Can they survive?
og_title: The Two Throws: An Immortal’s Legacy Defended by Ten Thousand Dao-Soldiers
og_description: A single, perfect throw shatters a thousand-strong demonic formation. But the victory is short-lived as a far greater threat emerges in Immortal Wu Jiang’s estate.
twitter_title: The Two Throws: A Xianxia Showdown at Immortal Wu Jiang’s Estate
twitter_description: Ji Ning’s party is crushed by a thousand Dao-soldiers. One expert’s two throws kill the commander and break the formation, but ten thousand more are coming. High-stakes action!

lore_anchors.definition: Specialized armor that synchronizes the Ki and Divine Power of all wearers, allowing them to function as a single, massive formation entity, multiplying their combat power drastically.
The key point of balance or flow in a formation; destroying it can collapse the entire structure, as Uncle Fang demonstrated with his first shuttle throw.
Dao-soldier armor designed for Wanxiang Adepts; each suit is more valuable than an Earth-ranked magic treasure due to its rarity and the power it provides.
A demonic beast that has reached the Primal Daoist stage, possessing immense power, divine sense, and the ability to lead armies.
A sword formation technique that allows a cultivator to control multiple flying swords in concert; Ji Ning uses its ninth layer here to form a single, massive sword of light.
A legendary nine-stance sword art from Immortal Beixing; Ji Ning uses the fifth stance ‘Moonlight Hides the Sword’ in this battle.

cultural_notes_faq.q: How did Uncle Fang kill the Primal-level demoness so easily?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is a peak-level combatant—likely a Primal Daoist himself, or close to it—who specializes in finding and breaking the ‘central node’ of formations. By shattering the Dao-soldier wave first, he removed the collective protection, then killed the exposed commander with a second throw.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn’t Shaoyin Nong use any of his treasures to save his Zifu Disciples?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is a cold, pragmatic noble. Treasures used early are treasures wasted. He views the Zifu Disciples as expendable cannon fodder and is hoarding his ace cards for the even greater dangers he knows lie deeper in the estate.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of the Dao-soldier armor loot?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is incredibly valuable, especially the Wanxiang-grade sets. This represents a major acquisition for Ji Ning and the others, providing them with either powerful gear or a huge amount of wealth to trade for other resources.
